release-deployment-safety.why: this IS a release: a backward-compatible version bump across all sources + CHANGELOG, with a provenance-safe publish order
release-deployment-safety.what: bumped package.json/VERSION/package-lock/gate-manifest to 1.1.0 (gates unchanged, backward-compatible: 1.0.0 consumers unaffected), wrote the 1.1.0 CHANGELOG, and sequenced the tag/asset publish so origin-mode provenance passes on the unpublished version before the release is cut
quotes: Every change must be independently deployable, backward-compatible, observable while it rolls out,

skeptical-audit.why: the CHANGELOG states the limits rather than overclaiming the adoption story
skeptical-audit.what: the 1.1.0 notes include an Honest limits section: a git pull arms nothing by itself (one npm install), a scaffolded CODEOWNERS is necessary but not sufficient, and the local pre-push runs the fast offline gates only
quotes: content hash, a query, a version/commit SHA, or a URL + retrieval date;

judge-arch.why: reviewed the release in fresh context before the PR
judge-arch.what: ran a fresh-context judge-arch over the version bump consistency and the CHANGELOG accuracy before opening the release PR
quotes: These are not optional and not left to discretion. Every review does all

architectural-decision-records.why: a release bump; it references existing ADRs 0051-0055, makes no new decision

verifiable-quality-gates.why: no gate added or changed; gate sha256s unchanged, re-verified they still pass after the bump
